segments.prompt:
2D hand-drawn cinematic single-character sequence, vertical 9:16, 15 seconds.

STYLE IDENTITY LOCK: preserve the verified drawing language, proportions, materials and original colors of Picture 1 and Picture 2. Keep the exact mouse-eared mutant girl's short white hair with eye-covering fringe and small upward curl, large translucent pale-violet mouse-ear structures, small slender body, oversized pale robe, dark collar, cuffs and hem blocks, diagonal strap and side satchel. Preserve the warm-sky and cool-lake palette relationship of the forest-lake scene. Reference fidelity overrides generic style wording.

VISUAL EXPRESSION VARIABLE: use restrained readable 2D motion, compatible variable-weight ink lines, thin watercolor-like shading only where consistent with the references, soft diffuse light, muted shadows and generous negative space over the water. Keep the action continuous and observational, never a rhythmic montage.

CHARACTER (Picture 1): show exactly one physical instance of the established mouse-eared mutant girl. If Picture 1 is a multi-view identity sheet, all views describe this one character and must not become multiple people. Preserve her quiet, cautious behavior and every verified clothing and accessory feature.

ENVIRONMENT (Picture 2): preserve the identity, existing lake, layered forest, spatial continuity and established warm-sky/cool-water color logic of SCENE-02. Picture 2 defines the place, not one mandatory framing. Do not invent a bridge, dock, stepping stones, exposed roots, buildings or props. The visible water reflection must be only the optical reflection of the same girl, physically dependent on her position and deformed only by the water surface.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION: use a medium-wide three-quarter side view on the lakeshore. Keep the single girl and her dependent water reflection readable in the same frame, with a narrow foreground shore edge, the girl and water in the middle ground, layered trees behind, and quiet negative space across the lake. Hold a stable camera; allow only a barely perceptible push after the water disturbance if the verified scene geometry supports it.

ACTION: the girl walks slowly along the shore at a safe distance from the water. Her dependent reflection follows directly beneath and beside her according to the water surface. One small natural ripple crosses the reflected outline and briefly displaces its shape without giving it independent motion. She notices the mismatch, stops, and takes one short half-step back from the water. Her near mouse-ear structure turns toward the ripple first while her torso, hands and feet become still; her eyes follow a moment later. End on a clear held pose: she has chosen not to leave, but has not approached the water.

AUDIO DESIGN: quiet lake air, faint leaves, soft water movement, light robe and strap friction, small careful footfalls and one close ripple at the visible distortion. A thin non-melodic low breath tone tightens at the reflection offset, falls almost silent on the half-step back, and remains suspended at the cut. Audio clarifies the event and caution; it does not set an MV beat.

NEGATIVE: no second physical character, no duplicate girl, clone, twin, separate water person, autonomous reflection, emerging reflection, independent shadow double, split screen or four-person character sheet; no rabbit ears, ordinary human ears replacing the mutation, tail, horns, wings, armor, weapon, fitted battle costume or adult muscular proportions; no complete reflection moving on its own or remaining delayed after the ripple passes; no invented bridge, dock, stones, roots, buildings or props; no dramatic splash, fall, run, panic, dance, lip-sync, speed ramp, montage or music-video cutting; no cyan-white energy humanoid, glossy 3D render, hard synthetic digital edges, text, subtitle, logo or watermark.

segments.prompt:
2D hand-drawn cinematic single-character sequence, vertical 9:16, 15 seconds, continuing directly from the selected real ending frame of Segment A.

STYLE IDENTITY LOCK: preserve the same verified Picture 1 identity, drawing language, proportions, materials and original colors, and preserve the same Picture 2 forest-lake identity and warm-sky/cool-water palette logic. Keep the girl's short white hair, eye-covering fringe, small upward curl, translucent pale-violet mouse-ear structures, small slender body, oversized pale robe, dark edge blocks, diagonal strap and side satchel exactly consistent with Segment A.

VISUAL EXPRESSION VARIABLE: use restrained readable 2D motion, compatible variable-weight linework, thin watercolor-like shading only where reference-consistent, soft diffuse light, muted shadows and controlled negative space. Let two small reversible tests and their pauses carry the character performance; avoid theatrical posing or rhythmic montage.

CHARACTER (Picture 1): show exactly the same one physical mouse-eared mutant girl from Segment A. Preserve the chosen real A ending pose, clothing state, satchel position and cautious expression. A multi-view reference still represents one identity only.

ENVIRONMENT (Picture 2): remain in the same verified SCENE-02 lakeshore space, with the same lake, layered forest, screen direction, lighting direction and established palette relationship. The water image is only the optically dependent reflection of this one girl; it must respond to her body and the water surface and must never behave as a separate entity. Do not add unverified shore objects or a reverse space.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION: inherit the exact camera side, axis, shoreline relation and character position from the selected real Segment A ending. Use a medium-full three-quarter side view that keeps her feet, the relevant water area and the dependent reflection readable together. A restrained lateral drift may follow her only if Picture 2 supports continuous shore space; otherwise keep the camera fixed. Never cross the axis.

ACTION: after the held ending of Segment A, the girl keeps her upper body quiet and makes one small lateral step away from the water. The dependent reflection shifts with her and settles as the last ripple fades. She pauses long enough to confirm the match. Her ears ease slightly. She then deliberately makes one equally small return step to her original walking line, watching the reflection align again. Hold one calm beat. Without approaching the water, she resumes her original slow direction along the shore for two measured steps. End with the reflection still causally aligned, her shoulders less tense, and her attention curious rather than alarmed.

AUDIO DESIGN: continue the same quiet lake air, faint leaves and soft water ambience from Segment A, adding two measured robe-softened side steps, subtle strap movement and the fading ripple. Use two very soft non-melodic tonal pulses triggered by the first lateral test and the return step; the second settles into a low quiet release as she resumes walking. Audio supports observation and emotional easing, never song structure or MV rhythm.

NEGATIVE: no second physical character, no duplicate girl, clone, twin, separate water person, autonomous reflection, emerging reflection, independent shadow double, split screen or four-person character sheet; no rabbit ears, ordinary human ears replacing the mutation, tail, horns, wings, armor, weapon, fitted battle costume or adult muscular proportions; no complete reflection moving before her, acting independently or staying delayed after the water settles; no invented bridge, dock, stones, roots, buildings, props or unseen reverse angle; no approach into the water, jump, run, dance, triumph pose, panic, lip-sync, speed ramp, montage or music-video cutting; no cyan-white energy humanoid, glossy 3D render, hard synthetic digital edges, text, subtitle, logo or watermark.
